title: Marcus-Stark field-robustness audit for low-offset OPV interface design
purpose: Test whether reducing reorganization energy at fixed Ex-to-CT driving force can increase sensitivity of the Marcus Ex-to-CT rate to field-induced CT-state energy shifts. This is a local normalized-rate robustness audit, not a device FF or Pmax predictor.

source_provenance.citation: Zhang et al., Overcoming the fill-factor limit of organic solar cells, Nature Photonics (2026)
used_for: bias-dependent PL and TDCF as field-dependence discriminators

source_provenance.citation: Luo et al., Suppressing electron-phonon coupling and energy loss in organic solar cells by modulating donor-acceptor penetrated-interface, Nature Communications 17, 2026 (2026)
used_for: existing commercial-bridge motivation linking penetrated interfaces, weaker EPC, and lower nonradiative voltage loss

source_provenance.note: The current linked repository is public and MATLAB-based. At this commit, functions/marcus_equation_stark.m visibly implements a quadratic polarizability Stark term. The Nature Photonics main text estimates the first-order dipole shift as approximately 35 meV and focuses Fig. 4g on the first-order effect. This project therefore independently implements the published equation/text for the first-order normalized-rate audit and does not claim a full reproduction of the authors' drift-diffusion code. No upstream code is copied.

equations.published_marcus_form: k(F) proportional to exp(-(lambda + DeltaG + delta(F))^2 / (4 lambda kB T))
equations.normalized_rate_ratio: R(delta)=k(delta)/k(0)=exp(-(2 A delta + delta^2)/(4 lambda kB T)), A=lambda+DeltaG
equations.activationless_limit: If DeltaG=-lambda, then A=0 and R_plus=R_minus=exp(-delta^2/(4 lambda kB T)).
equations.first_order_stark_energy: |delta|_eV = |F|_V_per_m * d_m for a one-electron charge separation

published_scale_anchor.classification: literature-derived approximate scale, not an R2/B0/B1/B2 measurement
published_scale_anchor.paper_description: approximately 1 V per 100 nm and approximately 3.5 nm CT separation, yielding approximately 35 meV first-order Stark shift

synthetic_fixture.note: DeltaG=-100 meV and the lambda grid are not claimed measured for D18/PY-IT/eC9. The 10/35/70 meV delta sweep is a sensitivity bracket, not a statistical uncertainty interval.

analytic_window_result.condition: For fixed DeltaG=-g<0 and 0<delta<2g, R_worst is maximized at lambda=g=-DeltaG.
analytic_window_result.interpretation: In this Marcus-Stark local robustness metric, the optimal reorganization energy is a matching window rather than lambda approaching zero. This does not establish that any real device has the same optimum.

prospective_program_narrowing.hypothesis: An interface modification that lowers EPC/reorganization and DeltaVnr may still fail useful-work validation if it increases field-dependent Ex-to-CT generation losses or reduces FF.
required_discriminator_before_strong_use: bias-dependent photoluminescence and/or TDCF or an independently justified equivalent field-dependence measurement
morphology/contact/transport controls already required by the program
prospective_program_narrowing.kill_or_narrow_rule: If an arm lowers DeltaVnr/Voc loss but shows materially worse field-dependent generation and fails to improve stabilized FF/Pmax, retain it as voltage-loss/mechanism science and do not promote it as useful-work or platform validation.
prospective_program_narrowing.threshold_policy: v3.45 does not invent a universal beta, R_worst, PL-quench, TDCF, or FF threshold. Physical thresholds must be prospectively frozen from measurement capability and baseline data.

validity_limits: Classical Marcus rate form only; MLJ, multimode vibronics, disorder, delocalization, back-transfer, exciton diffusion, and full device electrostatics are outside this local audit.
R_worst is a deliberately conservative local orientation diagnostic, not an orientationally averaged device generation yield.
Electronic coupling prefactors cancel only in the normalized comparison when the prefactor is held fixed.
The 35 meV literature scale is approximate and not a measured field shift for the D18/PY-IT/eC9 campaign.
No causal EPC, quantum advantage, FF improvement, Pmax improvement, or commercial performance is claimed.

required: direct exponent ratio agrees with closed form
finite-difference derivative agrees with analytic derivative
published field-distance scale independently reproduces 0.035 eV
synthetic optimization grid peaks at lambda=-DeltaG
